title: Learning Acrobatic Flight from Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2508.18817v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) enables agents to learn control policies without requiring manually designed reward functions, making it well-suited for tasks where objectives are difficult to formalize or inherently subjective. Acrobatic flight poses a particularly challenging problem due to its complex dynamics, rapid movements, and the importance of precise execution. However, manually designed reward functions for such tasks often fail to capture the qualities that matter: we find that hand-crafted rewards agree with human judgment only 60.7% of the time, underscoring the need for preference-driven approaches. In this work, we propose Reward Ensemble under Confidence (REC), a probabilistic reward learning framework for PbRL that explicitly models per-timestep reward uncertainty through an ensemble of distributional reward models. translated_title: 从偏好中学习特技飞行
translated_abstract: 基于偏好的强化学习使智能体能够在无需人工设计奖励函数的情况下学习控制策略，因此非常适合那些目标难以形式化或本质上具有主观性的任务。特技飞行是一个特别具有挑战性的问题，因为其动力学复杂、运动速度快，且精确执行至关重要。然而，为此类任务人工设计的奖励函数往往无法捕捉真正重要的品质：我们发现手工设计的奖励与人类判断仅有60.7%的一致率，这凸显了基于偏好方法的必要性。在本工作中，我们提出了置信度下的奖励集成，这是一种用于偏好强化学习的概率性奖励学习框架，通过分布奖励模型的集成显式地对每个时间步的奖励不确定性进行建模。该方法将不确定性传播到偏好损失中，并利用模型间的分歧（来指导策略学习）。
tldr: 本文提出REC框架，通过集成分布奖励模型显式建模每个时间步的奖励不确定性，解决了手工设计奖励函数与人类判断不一致的问题，使智能体能够仅凭人类偏好学会执行高难度的特技飞行动作。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes REC, a probabilistic reward learning framework that explicitly models per-timestep reward uncertainty through ensembles of distributional reward models, enabling agents to learn challenging acrobatic flight solely from human preferences, overcoming the limitations of hand-crafted reward functions.
